```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(pdmS7)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This page is the reference: every equation pdmS7 implements, with Moore (2007) equation
numbers for the PDM; the snow model follows equations 2.1 to 2.8 of the Institute of
Hydrology PACK report. Notes mark where the implementation interprets or corrects the
source. For what the equations *mean*,
start with [How the PDM works](pdm-explained.html) and
[How the snow model works](snowpack-explained.html).

# Units and symbols

All depths are millimetres averaged over the catchment; time is in hours internally.

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $p$, $e$, $d$, $v$ | Rain, actual evaporation, recharge and runoff depths per interval | mm |
| $s$ | Catchment-average soil water | mm |
| $c$ | A local store's capacity | mm |
| $C$ | Common filling level of the stores | mm |
| $F(c)$ | Fraction of the catchment with capacity no greater than $c$ | fraction |
| $X$, $u$, $q$ | Routing storage, inflow rate and outflow rate | mm; mm/h; mm/h |
| $\Delta t$ | Model interval | h |
| $A$ | Catchment area | km² |

Rain and potential evaporation are interval totals, not rates. `q_m3s` is the mean flow over
the interval; `q_end_m3s` is the flow at its end.

# PDM

## Soil moisture: the capacity distribution (Eq. 2-3, 7, 9, 18-20)

For a filling level $C$, the fraction of the catchment that is saturated is $F(C)$, and the
mean water stored across the catchment is

$$s(C)=\int_0^C [1-F(c)]\,dc, \qquad s_{\max}=E[c].$$

`capacity_cdf()` returns $F(C)$; `storage_from_capacity()` evaluates $s(C)$ and
`capacity_from_storage()` inverts it; `capacity_mean()` returns $s_{\max}$, the mean
capacity, which is not the largest local capacity.

With $a=c_{\min}$, $z=c_{\max}$ and $w=z-a$, the five capacity families are:

| Family (`type`) | CDF inside its support | Mean capacity |
|---|---|---|
| Pareto (`pareto`) | $1-[(z-c)/w]^b$ | $a+w/(b+1)$ |
| Rectangular (`rectangular`) | $(c-a)/w$ | $(a+z)/2$ |
| Symmetric triangular (`triangular`) | $2(c-a)^2/w^2$ below the midpoint; $1-2(z-c)^2/w^2$ above | $(a+z)/2$ |
| Exponential (`exponential`) | $1-\exp(-c/\mu)$ for $c\ge 0$ | $\mu$ |
| Lognormal (`lognormal`) | $\Phi((\log c-\mu_L)/\sigma_L)$ for $c>0$ | $\exp(\mu_L+\sigma_L^2/2)$ |

$\Phi$ is the standard normal CDF. CDFs are zero below and one above a bounded support.
Pareto with $b=0$ is a point mass at $c_{\max}$. The printed Appendix A formulas for the
rectangular and triangular families assume $c_{\min}=0$; pdmS7 uses the general forms above.
The triangular and lognormal storage functions are inverted exactly (cubic solution, and
Newton iteration from a bracket); see `source-notes.md`.

## Evaporation, recharge and runoff (Eq. 5-8, 10, 15-17)

Rain is first multiplied by the rainfall factor: $p=f_c\,p_{\mathrm{input}}$. With soil
storage $s$ at the start of the interval and potential evaporation $e_p$:

$$e_{\mathrm{req}}=e_p\left[1-\left(1-\frac{s}{s_{\max}}\right)^{b_e}\right].\qquad\text{(Eq. 8)}$$

Evaporation is allocated first and recharge second, so neither can overdraw the store:

$$e=\min(e_{\mathrm{req}},\,s+p),\qquad d=\min(d_{\mathrm{req}},\,\max(0,\,s+p-e)).$$

The net depth $n=p-e-d$ fills the stores. When $n>0$,

$$C=s^{-1}(s_{\mathrm{old}}),\quad s_{\mathrm{new}}=s(C+n),\quad
v=n-(s_{\mathrm{new}}-s_{\mathrm{old}}).\qquad\text{(Eq. 15-17)}$$

Whatever cannot be stored becomes direct runoff $v$. When $n\le 0$ storage falls and runoff
is zero.

## Recharge (Eq. 10-13)

**Standard** recharge drains soil water above a threshold $s_t$:

$$d_{\mathrm{req}}=\frac{\max(0,\,s-s_t)^{b_g}}{k_g}\,\Delta t.\qquad\text{(Eq. 10)}$$

$k_g$ has units h·mm$^{b_g-1}$, which are hours only when $b_g=1$.

**Demand** recharge depends on the groundwater deficit. With $X_{\max}$ the groundwater
storage giving outflow $q_{\mathrm{sat}}$, $g=\min(1,\max(0,(X_{\max}-X)/X_{\max}))$ and
$d_{\mathrm{sat}}=q_{\mathrm{sat}}\Delta t$:

$$d_{\mathrm{req}}=\left[d_{\mathrm{sat}}+(s_{\max}-d_{\mathrm{sat}})
\min\left(1,(g/\alpha)^\beta\right)\right]\frac{s}{s_{\max}}.\qquad\text{(Eq. 11-13)}$$

This is written as a depth per interval, so it depends on the time step, and it needs
$q_{\mathrm{sat}}\Delta t\le s_{\max}$ and a single groundwater store.

**Split** recharge has no soil drainage: direct runoff is divided, $\alpha v$ to the surface
store and $(1-\alpha)v$ to groundwater.

## Routing (Eq. 21-27)

Each routing store obeys

$$\frac{dX}{dt}=u-q(X).\qquad\text{(Eq. 21-23)}$$

| Option | Outflow law | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Linear | $q=X/k_b$ | Exact solution |
| Quadratic | $q=X^2/k_b$ | Exact solution |
| Cubic | $q=X^3/k_b$ | Adaptive integration; optional Smith recurrence (Eq. 24-25) |
| Power | $q=kX^m$ | Adaptive integration (Eq. 21-23) |
| Cascade | $\dot X_1=u-X_1/k_1$, $\dot X_2=X_1/k_1-X_2/k_2$ | Exact two-store solution (Eq. 26-27) |
| Exponential | $q=\exp(\gamma+aX)$ | $X$ is a signed log-storage coordinate, not a tank |

Inflow is constant within an interval. The Smith recurrence is accurate only for steps up
to about an hour; see [Choosing model components](model-options.html).

## Delay and discharge

After an outlet delay $t_d$ (fractional delays split water between neighbouring intervals),
the mean flow is

$$Q_{\mathrm{mean}}=\frac{A}{3.6}\,\frac{V_{\mathrm{fast}}+V_{\mathrm{slow}}}{\Delta t}+q_c,$$

where $V$ are the routed depths in mm over the interval and $q_c$ is a constant external
adjustment in m³/s that does not draw on the model's stores.

## Water balance

$$\epsilon=\text{old storage}+p-e-\text{natural outflow}-\text{new storage},$$

with storage including the soil, routing stores and water in the delay queue. pdmS7 reports
$\epsilon$ for every step; it is zero to rounding.

## Forecast updating (Eq. 28-42)

State correction (Eq. 28-30) distributes the flow error at the forecast origin between the
surface and groundwater stores, with gains, in proportional, super-proportional or
non-proportional form; ARMA error prediction (Eq. 31-42) forecasts the error series in
additive or log form, with pdmS7's `ar` equal to $-\phi$ in Moore's notation. See
[Forecast updating](forecast-updating.html).

# PACK snow model

## Rain or snow

With corrected precipitation $p$, temperature $T$ and snow threshold $T_s$:

$$p_{\mathrm{snow}}=\begin{cases}p,&T<T_s\\0,&T\ge T_s\end{cases},\qquad
p_{\mathrm{rain}}=p-p_{\mathrm{snow}}.$$

New snow enters the dry store $W$ and restores full cover.

## Melt

With snow-covered fraction $F$, melt factor $f$, melt threshold $T_m$ and internal step $h$:

$$m=\min\left(W+p_{\mathrm{snow}},\;F f\max(0,T-T_m)\,h\right),\qquad
W_{\mathrm{new}}=W+p_{\mathrm{snow}}-m.$$

## Liquid water and drainage

Rain on covered ground and meltwater enter the wet store $S$:

$$S'=S+F p_{\mathrm{rain}}+m,\qquad S_c=r\,(S'+W_{\mathrm{new}}).$$

$$D=\begin{cases}0,&T<T_c\\
\min\{S',\;h[k_1S'+k_2\max(S'-S_c,0)]\},&T\ge T_c\end{cases}$$

$$S_{\mathrm{new}}=S'-D,\qquad p_{\mathrm{effective}}=D+(1-F)\,p_{\mathrm{rain}}.$$

Cold weather stops drainage but does not refreeze liquid water.

## Snow cover (PACK Figure 2.2)

With total water content $\theta=W+S$ and $\theta_c$ the content for complete cover:

$$F_0(\theta)=\min\left(1,\frac{\log(1+\theta)}{\log(1+\theta_c)}\right).$$

After fresh snow, cover returns to $F_0$ along a path anchored at the previous content
$\theta_a$ and cover $F_a$, over the final fraction $\alpha$ of the fresh-snow excursion $N$:

$$F(\theta)=\max\left[F_0(\theta),\;F_a+(1-F_a)\min\left(1,\frac{\theta-\theta_a}{\alpha N}\right)\right]
\quad\text{for }\theta>\theta_a.$$

The report gives prose and a diagram rather than full event logic; pdmS7's reading is
recorded in `source-notes.md`.

## Internal steps and balance

Each interval is divided into

$$N_{\mathrm{sub}}=\left\lceil\max\left(\frac{60\,\Delta t}{\text{max\_step\_min}},\;
\Delta t\,(k_1+k_2),\;1\right)\right\rceil$$

steps to keep the drainage calculation stable. The snow balance residual is

$$\epsilon_{\mathrm{snow}}=(W+S)_{\mathrm{old}}+p_{\mathrm{corrected}}
-p_{\mathrm{effective}}-(W+S)_{\mathrm{new}}.$$

When PACK feeds the PDM, the PDM's $f_c$ still multiplies the effective rain; set it to 1 to
avoid correcting precipitation twice.

- Moore, R. J. (2007). The PDM rainfall-runoff model. *Hydrology and Earth System Sciences*,

- Institute of Hydrology. *PACK: A Pragmatic Snowmelt Model for Real-time Use.*
  [NORA 15304](https://nora.nerc.ac.uk/id/eprint/15304/1/N015304CR.pdf), equations 2.1-2.8,
  Figure 2.2 and Table 2.1.
- `source-notes.md` in the package source records every interpretation and correction.
